neighboring_unit_entries.title: Logarithmic-derivative negativity propagates left-side zero finiteness
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Expands a derivative's logarithmic derivative over real and nonreal zeros, observes that only finitely many left-side nonreal terms are bounded while the real-zero sum becomes logarithmically negative, excludes new far-left nonreal zeros of the next derivative, and iterates; under RH this closes the higher-derivative moment formula.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Boxes around right-side zeta zeros identify where logarithmic-derivative positivity can fail; chaining overlapping protruding boxes and applying Littlewood's lemma only on those rectangles converts a density estimate for zeta zeros into quantitative and qualitative scarcity of far-left zeta-prime zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The result is conditional on the cited density input and source ranges; formula OCR prevents safe reuse of exact numerical exponents without the scan.
